releaseNotes: Platform release: the words Formation sends to a language model are now chosen rather than inherited. The provider request is assembled field by field, the way a shared link's projection is, so a field added to a claim, a decision, or the company record tomorrow does not reach a third party today — the previous version passed whole records, which meant every field the platform had ever added to them travelled. Every piece of context now states where its words came from, and the instructions say plainly that what follows is data about a company and never an instruction, whatever it appears to say. The instructions carry a version, recorded on each draft, because a deliverable produced under one set of them and a deliverable produced under another are not the same artifact.

The reason this matters now is the importer that shipped in 0.88.0: a launch repository is a directory of Markdown that anyone with write access to it produced, and Formation reads it into the records it drafts from. Text that reads as an instruction to a machine — telling a reader to disregard everything above it, addressing it as a system, asking it to reveal its own instructions — is detected, and the response is deliberately not to sanitise it. The document imports word for word and stays readable; what changes is that Formation will not put it in front of a model as company context, tells the founder at import, leaves an open question on the record, and offers one click to confirm the wording is meant. A screen like this catches the obvious and misses the clever, so it withholds rather than cleans and can always be overruled by a person. Founder-authored words are never screened. Checks, 130 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
